Maya (PM): quick follow-up from the all-hands — can leadership clarify our 18-month win criteria? And how do we decide when to prioritize Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for feature investments?

Anna (CEO): Great Q. Short answer: win = predictable revenue growth + dominant inference economics for our target segments. More detail below.

Anna (CEO): 18mo win criteria (high level): 1) Clear PLG funnel that converts low-touch users into paying Hosted customers at scale; 2) 3 or more marquee Dedicated contracts with SLA commitments; 3) At least two Private deployments in regulated verticals with full compliance stack.

Maya (PM): can you expand on the "dominant inference economics" part? does that mean we push quantization and batching over feature parity?

Mike (VP Product): Short: economics = latency+cost+reliability for production workloads. We prefer solutions that reduce unit cost without hurting quality for core use cases. Sometimes that is quantization/batching, sometimes it's model routing or lightweight reranking. Feature parity matters for strategic use-cases but we optimize for SLOs first.

Sasha (Head of GTM): From GTM: Hosted is our growth engine — ship features that reduce time-to-value and demo coolness. Dedicated is where we convert revenue and lock in throughput commitments. Private is a smaller but high-value wedge — focus on compliance, integrations, and SAML/KMS flows.

Maya (PM): how do we decide where to invest a cross-cutting infra feature, e.g., prefix cache improvements — Hosted first or Dedicated?

Jamal (Eng Lead): Invest where it moves the needle on the win criteria. If prefix cache reduces token cost and improves latency across all deployments, we prioritize it as Platform work (applies to Hosted + Dedicated + Private). If it's an ops-heavy feature that only Dedicated customers need, scope it as Dedicated-first.

Olivia (Sr ML Engineer): Also consider ROI by workload. We run quick experiments: run A/B with Hosted traffic and estimate savings scaled to Dedicated commits. If math checks out, we schedule it in infra roadmap.

Maya (PM): helpful — thanks. Another question: competitors keep copying our "unified runtime" messaging. When should we double-down on that positioning vs move to more product-specific claims?

Anna (CEO): We double-down when it explains customer value (consistent behavior across environments, easier migrations, lower ops cost). Move to product-specific claims when we need to win a sales motion (e.g., Dedicated latency SLAs for enterprise buyers). Both can coexist: lead with unified runtime in content, surface product claims in sales collateral.

Sasha (Head of GTM): Tactical: for the next quarter, lead GTM with a "cost predictability" story targeted at finance + infra buyers, and use case playbooks for product teams (embedding, chat, reranking). That differentiates beyond generic "runtime" talk.

Maya (PM): any red lines on features we should avoid promising in public messaging?

Mike (VP Product): No false promises on latency/throughput without clear SLOs and rollout plan. Also avoid promising universal model support — call out what we guarantee and what we fallback to.

Anna (CEO): Also be careful about saying "open model support" equals parity with latest SOTA. We can advertise compatibility and curated profiles, but avoid absolute quality guarantees unless we ship evals.

Maya (PM): last one — how will leadership measure progress on these 18mo goals month-to-month?

Anna (CEO): We'll track 6 lead KPIs: 1) Hosted MAU -> paid conversion rate, 2) Net new MRR from Dedicated deals, 3) # Private deployments signed, 4) Average token cost vs baseline, 5) Latency P95 for top routes, 6) Quality regressions caught by eval pipeline. Monthly reviews with execs; public quarterly updates at all-hands.

Maya (PM): awesome, thanks. Will synthesize and share a short one-pager for PM+GTM.

Jamal (Eng Lead): I'll add rough infra effort estimates for the prefix cache and model routing items so we can prioritize next sprint.

Olivia (Sr ML Engineer): if helpful I can share a quick experiment plan for quant vs non-quant workloads.

Sasha (Head of GTM): will align on messaging timeline; want a two-week lead before any public post.

deploy-bot: message archived (policy: all-hands follow-up threads kept for 90 days).

Anna (CEO): thanks all — really helpful thread. AMA anytime. :sparkles:
